Title: Parang-wielding duo rob taxi driver, friend during drinks outside eatery
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A taxi driver and his female friend were held at knifepoint by two men who robbed them of cash and valuables worth about RM3,000 while they were having drinks outside an eatery here recently.
The incident occurred about 4am last Saturday when the 57-year-old man, who only wanted to be identified as Kong, and his 48-year-old female friend were having drinks and chatting outside the eatery in Jalan Riang Ria, Happy Garden, here.
Kong said more than 10 of his friends had been at the eatery earlier, but they gradually left, leaving him and his friend behind.
"By about 4am, there were hardly any people around. Suddenly, two men barged towards us and held parangs to our necks, ordering us not to move and demanding that we hand over our valuables.
"They took our handbags and wallets, causing us to lose RM1,100 in cash, mobile phones, car keys and identification documents, with total losses estimated at about RM3,000," he said when contacted today.
He said among the items stolen was his friend's mobile phone, which she had bought only about two months ago.
Kong added that both suspects were wearing helmets, making it difficult to see their faces clearly.
"They then fled towards the end of the lane, but it was dark and we could not see which direction they took," he said.
Kong said his friend later recalled seeing one of the suspects entering and leaving an electronic gaming centre next to the eatery several days before the robbery.
"She told me that after the incident, the suspect had been loitering around the area. Perhaps they were already looking for a target to rob at the time," he said.
He said the operators of the eatery and the electronic gaming centre had also handed CCTV footage to police.
"The CCTV footage showed that the suspects had been in the area and loitering there for quite some time before the incident.
"The entire incident happened quickly, but fortunately, my friend and I were not injured," he said.
Meanwhile, Brickfields district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook confirmed that a report had been lodged and the case was being investigated under Sections 395/397 of the Penal Code for gang robbery and robbery with a weapon.
"Efforts to track down the suspects are ongoing," he said.

Title: Man drowns during outing with 13 friends at forest reserve waterfall
Article:
BENTONG: A day out for 14 friends turned tragic when one of them drowned at the Chamang Forest Reserve waterfall here today.
Mohd Aiman Nazmi Mohd Yusuf, 29, from Felda Endau, Johor, was pronounced dead at the scene.
Pahang Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Mohd Salahuddin Isa said the department received an emergency call about the incident at 1.29pm.
"Firemen arrived at 2.11pm and were informed that a man had drowned after visiting the recreational area with 13 friends.
"The group comprised eight men and five women from Coffee Bean Caltex Sungai Besi," he said.
Salahuddin said forestry officers had managed to retrieve the victim about 20 metres from where he was reported to have gone missing in the waterfall before the firemen arrived.
He said Health Ministry personnel who also arrived at the scene later confirmed that the victim had died.
"All 13 of the victim's friends were reported safe. The victim's body was later handed over to the police," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: KLVC land deal: Ex-senior Felda officer to be charged tomorrow [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A former senior Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) officer, who was previously investigated over the alleged misappropriation of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project, will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow.
Based on a court system check, the man will be charged in Criminal Sessions Court 14 before Judge Suzana Hussin at 9am.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) confirmed that it had obtained approval to charge the former Felda officer.
On Sept 25, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the individual would face one charge under Section 420 of the Penal Code.
The KLVC investigation is part of seven investigation papers involving Felda and Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), comprising six new investigation papers and one previous investigation.
The investigations focus on the purchase and investment of assets by Felda and FIC between 2010 and 2020, which are suspected to involve corruption, misappropriation and abuse of power.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man held with 2,000 suspected yaba pills in Gua Musang
Article:
GUA MUSANG: Police arrested a 49-year-old man and seized about 2,000 pills believed to be yaba, weighing 200g and estimated to be worth RM30,000, during a check at Km18 of Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Lipis yesterday.
Gua Musang district police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo said the suspect was arrested about 6pm after allegedly attempting to flee when his Toyota Vios was stopped for checks by a mobile patrol vehicle (MPV) unit from the Gua Musang District Police Headquarters.
He said police pursued and detained the suspect before searching the vehicle and discovering the suspected yaba pills.
"A preliminary urine screening test found the suspect positive for methamphetamine," he said in a statement today.
Sik said police also seized the car, a car key and two mobile phones to assist in the investigation.
The case is being investigated under Sections 39B and 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
Investigations are ongoing.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Slovak school stabbing kills teacher, injures two
Article:
BRATISLAVA: A knife-wielding schoolboy killed a teacher and wounded another and a pupil in an attack in northwestern Slovakia on Tuesday, authorities said.
The attack occurred at around 0700 GMT in the village of Staskov, close to the Czech border.
A 13-year-old schoolboy was detained over the attack, police said, adding that he was being investigated for murder.
"This morning, after the first class, a school pupil launched a knife attack," Interior Minister Matus Sutaj Estok told reporters.
A 61-year-old woman died of her injuries, while a 44-year-old "with a stab wound to the chest" and a girl were hospitalised, emergency service spokeswoman Petra Klimesova told AFP.
The schoolgirl was "in a serious, critical condition, in a state of heavy neuralgic shock" after the attack, Health Minister Kamil Sasko told reporters.
Sutaj Estok said later that the injured teacher's life was not in danger.
Police said the situation in the village was "under control."
Asked by journalists, Education Minister Tomas Drucker declined to say whether the attack was due to bullying.
'Tragic incident'
Nationalist Prime Minister Robert Fico expressed his "sincere condolences" and said he was following "the tragic incident in the village of Staskov with great concern."
"Personally, I am deeply saddened by this," he said in a statement.
President Peter Pellegrini said he was "shocked that this is yet another case in which a student attacked teachers and a classmate."
"Aggression and an atmosphere of intolerance – spread primarily by social media and, unfortunately, by some politicians as well – are literally poisoning the public sphere and influencing the behaviour of our children in schools," he said.
He urged "all citizens to act in a way that calms the atmosphere, rather than further radicalising it."
In January last year, an 18-year-old killed a fellow pupil and a teacher in a knife attack and wounded another pupil at a secondary school in the town of Spisska Stara Ves in northeastern Slovakia.
In 2020, a teacher was stabbed to death and several others wounded at an elementary school in central Slovakia, the first violent attack at a school in the central European EU and Nato member of 5.4 million people.

Title: Orphaned siblings killed days after asking photographer to reprint family photos
Article:
KANGAR: A 42-year-old man and his sister were killed when the motorcycle they were travelling on collided with a multi-purpose vehicle (MPV) on Jalan Kuala Perlis-Changlun near Bukit Mas here today.
The victims in the 8.25am accident were identified as Ahmad Rifaie, 42, and his sister, Hakimah Zambri, 33.
Their deaths have left their family devastated, as the siblings had lived independently and relied on each other since their parents died.
Their uncle, Abd Malik Yahaya, 55, said he never expected Hakimah's visit to his home yesterday to be their last meeting.
"They had lived independently since their parents died. Their father died when Hakimah was still in primary school, while their mother died in 2013.
"In fact, relatives from their father's side had also visited them at home only yesterday," he said when met at the Forensic Medicine Department of Hospital Tuanku Fauziah  here today.
Abd Malik said Hakimah and Ahmad Rifaie were among four siblings, but only one is now left after their second brother died in December last year.
Meanwhile, PASTI Al Huda Pauh Putra photographer Nidzuwan Zainal Abidin, 52, also shared his grief, saying Hakimah had recently asked him to reprint old family photographs as keepsakes.
"I had often dealt with her to photograph PASTI programmes since 2018, and she was very cooperative in various matters.
"When I heard about her death, I was shocked, especially as she had only recently handed me old family photographs to be reprinted. Now, only one of her siblings remains," he said.
Hakimah had served as a teacher at PASTI since 2018.
Arau district police chief Superintendent Ahmad Mohsin Md Rodi said the accident was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Kim Loong lowers production target by 6 pct to 310,000 tonnes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Kim Loong Resources Bhd had lowered its production target for fresh fruit bunches (FFB) of oil palm by six per cent to 310,000 tonnes for the financial year ending Jan 31, 2027 (FY27).
The revised target came after considering the lower-than-expected FFB production achieved in the first half of the year to July 31, as well as the improved age profile of young productive palms and on-going replanting programme, it said.
"The group targets to replant about 700 hectares in the financial year 2027," said Kim Loong, in a filing with Bursa Malaysia announcing its financial results for the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q2 FY27).
During the quarter, Kim Loong registered five per cent lower net profits of RM44.94 million, compared with RM47.3 million in the corresponding quarter, on the back of three per cent lower revenue of RM422.76 million.
The lower revenue was partly due to the 17 per cent decline in FFB production during the quarter, to 72,438 tonnes, resulting in 15 per cent lower yield per hectare of 5.23 tonnes. Nevertheless, 14 per cent higher average FFB price during the quarter softened the impact.
Despite the weak performance in Q2, Kim Loong's first half net profits were 12 per cent higher, at RM100.12 million, due to its better first quarter results. Kim Loong declared an interim single tier dividend of five sen for FY27.
While projecting a lower FFB production this year, Kim Loong expects to achieve an optimum processing throughput of 1.6 million tonnes for its palm oil million operations.
Kim Loong expects the impact of lower FFB production target wil be partly cushioned by better crude palm oil (CPO) average price. The group expects the average CPO price to hover between RM4,500 and RM4,800 per tonne in FY27.

Title: Air Astana to launch Almaty-Langkawi flights in December
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air Astana will launch seasonal direct flights between Almaty and Langkawi from Dec 25, 2026 to March 27, 2027, marking the Kazakh flag carrier's return to Malaysia with its own scheduled services.
The Kazakhstan flag carrier said it has opened bookings for the new service, which will operate three times weekly on Tuesdays, Fridays and Sundays using an Airbus A321LR (long-range).
Flight KC8167 will depart Almaty at 9.35pm and arrive in Langkawi at 8.10am the following day, with a flight time of seven hours and 35 minutes.
The return flight, KC8168, will leave Langkawi at 9.40am and arrive in Almaty at 2.40pm, with a flight time of eight hours.
Air Astana said return fares start at US$740 in economy class and US$2,006 in business class, inclusive of taxes and charges.
Kazakh citizens can enter Malaysia without a visa for stays of up to 30 days.
"Langkawi is one of Malaysia's most popular island destinations, located in the Andaman Sea and known for its white-sand beaches, ancient mangrove forests and mountainous landscape," Air Astana said in a statement today.
The Langkawi service will reconnect Air Astana directly with Malaysia after the airline previously operated flights between Almaty and Kuala Lumpur.
Air Astana launched its first direct Almaty-Kuala Lumpur flight in October 2009.
However, the carrier suspended the direct flight in March 2020.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Newsweek ranks Sunway Medical Centre No. 1 in Malaysia for paediatrics
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sunway Medical Centre in has been ranked No. 1 in Malaysia for paediatrics in Newsweek's World's Best Specialised Hospitals 2027, marking its first inclusion in the global ranking.
The hospital was also recognised for oncology and neurology, with the ranking covering 13 medical specialities worldwide.
Sunway Medical Centre said the recognition comes as it expands its paediatric services with the opening of Tower F, a dedicated 216-bed children's tower.
The new tower expands the centre's paediatric services, including specialised inpatient care and subspecialties, while complementing its children's health and development Centre, paediatric intensive care unit and 24-hour children's walk-in and emergency department.
Sunway Healthcare Group president Datuk Lau Beng Long said the recognition reflected the hospital's progress in paediatrics, oncology and neurology.
"This recognition in paediatrics is particularly meaningful and timely as we mark the opening of our purpose-built 216-bedded Children's Tower, which brings together paediatric subspecialty services, including paediatric haematology and oncology, supported by a multidisciplinary paediatric team," he said.
Sunway Medical Centre chief executive officer Erica Lam said the recognition reaffirmed the hospital's focus on specialised and patient-centred care.
The latest ranking also placed the centre at No. 1 in Malaysia for neurology and recognised its oncology services.
Sunway Medical Centre said the Newsweek ranking assesses hospitals based on international peer recommendations, speciality-specific accreditations and certifications and the implementation of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures.
The hospital, which is the flagship of Sunway Healthcare Group, has more than 300 resident medical consultants across 80 medical specialities and 28 centres of excellence.
Following the opening of Tower F, its licensed bed capacity has increased to 961 beds.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Malaysia Airlines expands codeshare partnership with China Southern
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Airlines and China Southern Airlines will expand their codeshare partnership to cover five additional routes between Malaysia and China from Oct 25.
The expanded cooperation will connect Kuala Lumpur with Shenzhen, Changsha, Xiamen, Chengdu and Zhengzhou, giving passengers more travel options across the two airlines' networks.
Under the arrangement, both airlines will place their respective flight codes on eligible services operated by either carrier, allowing for smoother connections between their networks.
The expansion means all Kuala Lumpur-related routes operated by the two airlines between Malaysia and China will now be covered by the codeshare arrangement, including services to Guangzhou, Beijing Daxing, Shanghai Pudong, Shenzhen, Changsha, Xiamen, Chengdu Tianfu and Zhengzhou.
Malaysia Airlines and China Southern first launched their codeshare cooperation on the Kuala Lumpur-Guangzhou route in July 2023, before expanding it to Kuala Lumpur-Beijing Daxing, Kuala Lumpur-Shanghai Pudong and Penang-Guangzhou in July 2024.
Malaysia Airlines has also launched new services from Kuala Lumpur to Chengdu, Shenzhen and Changsha this year, while China Southern has increased capacity on its Kuala Lumpur-Guangzhou and Kuala Lumpur-Shenzhen routes.
Malaysia Aviation Group president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said the expanded partnership would strengthen Malaysia Airlines' connectivity with China.
"China remains a key strategic market for Malaysia Airlines, and our continued expansion in the country reflects the importance we place on strengthening our connections with the region," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: VS narrows net loss in Q4 to RM22mil as revenue rises
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: VS Industry Bhd reported a smaller net loss of RM22 million in the fourth quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q4 FY26), than RM33 million a year earlier, as revenue increased 16.3 per cent year-on-year to RM998.6 million.
The increase in revenue during the quarter was supported by higher sales orders from key customers despite higher impairment loss on plant and equipment amounting to RM39.7 million, said VS in a filing with Bursa Malaysia.
However, the electronic manufacturing services group recorded a net loss of RM53.82 million for FY26, compared with a net profit of RM36.71 million a year earlier, as VS is affected by lower orders from key customers affected by soft consumer sentiments globally, it said.
VS Industry said the weaker order intake affected overall production capacity utilisation, while customers also implemented cost optimisation measures.
Revenue for the year slipped 3.6 per cent to RM3.65 billion from RM3.78 billion.
VS Industry did not declare a dividend for the quarter, bringing its total dividend for FY26 to 0.4 sen per share, or RM15.4 million.
Managing director Datuk S Y Gan said persistent global trade uncertainties and weak consumer demand had characterised much of the financial year.
He said customer orders had started to pick up ahead of the year-end festive season, with the group expecting the positive momentum to continue into the next quarter.
"Moreover, our customers are planning to roll out new models in the coming fiscal year to maintain market competitiveness.
"Over in the Philippines, the operations continued to make progress, with a higher utilisation rate as additional models entered production.
"While the plant has yet to reach the breakeven point required to cover fixed costs, utilisation has improved on the back of higher production output," he said.

Title: UiTM Holdings losses not unknown to university management, says former VC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Financial problems affecting UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, which resulted in millions of ringgit in losses, were not unknown to the university's management but had been discussed and monitored at the highest levels, a former university vice-chancellor said.
Professor Datuk Dr Roziah Mohd Janor said UiTM Holdings' management was required to regularly present financial reports to the company's board of directors before they were brought to the university management and Board of Directors.
"The management was aware of the matter, and the crisis faced by UiTM Holdings had been discussed at the university management level.
"They had also been audited by a special audit team as well as the National Audit Department. However, during my tenure as vice-chancellor, I requested that every investment and project under UiTM Holdings be presented," she said.
Roziah said the public needed to understand that UiTM Holdings was a holding company owned by the university and that its initial capital did not come from direct government contributions or allocations.
Instead, she said, the capital came from internal accumulated funds generated and collected by the university.
She said regulatory mechanisms had also been established at the university's highest level to monitor investment governance and risks.
"The governance of UiTM's Board of Directors, both during my tenure and now, is supported by UiTM Board of Directors committees, which have a specific role in monitoring the company's operations and investment risks.
"In my view, UiTM is now improving the situation, and follow-up action must be actively undertaken by the current management and board of directors to address the issue," she said.
Roziah said the issue of UiTM Holdings' losses should be viewed alongside efforts to rehabilitate the company and improve its governance to safeguard the university's interests.
She said recommendations for improvement made through the audit process and the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) should be given attention and implemented immediately.
In March 2024, PAC found that UiTM Holdings and its subsidiaries had yet to achieve their original objectives and mandate of creating wealth for UiTM, creating investment opportunities and strengthening the strategic position of the company's core businesses.
The PAC also found that capital injections totalling RM259.98 million by UiTM between 2007 and 2018 for its shareholding in UiTM Holdings were not in accordance with the Universiti Teknologi MARA Act 1976 as they had not obtained the approval of the Finance Minister.
The committee, among other recommendations, called on UiTM to tighten oversight of UiTM Holdings and ensure compliance in matters involving investments, loans and the establishment of subsidiaries.
The issue came under renewed scrutiny after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim last Saturday called for
UiTM Holdings' management and governance
to be reviewed.
He had said that weaknesses needed to be rectified, while firm action should be taken if any wrongdoing was found.
The Higher Education Ministry also said the process of reviewing and restructuring the holding companies of public universities, including UiTM Holdings, had begun last year to ensure the entities functioned more effectively and contributed to their respective universities.
UiTM Holdings was previously reported to have recorded cumulative pre-tax losses of about RM157 million for the 2017, 2018, 2019 and 2021 financial years.
The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission also confirmed that an investigation launched in 2023 was still ongoing, including into issues related to the 50-megawatt solar project in Gambang, Pahang, and governance weaknesses that had been raised.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Crescendo's Q2 net profit more than quadruples on data centre land sale
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Crescendo Corporation Bhd recorded a net profit of RM70.6 million for the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q2 FY27), more than four times the level in the same quarter last year, boosted by the land sales to data centre developers in Kota Tinggi, Johor.
The net profit came on the back of a 158 per cent surge in revenue to RM210.43 million in Q2 FY27, Crescendo said in Bursa Malaysia filing.
The company announced a second-quarter dividend of two sen a share, scheduled for payment on Nov 12.
Proceeds from the sale of the lands led to a 263 per cent rise in revenue for the first half to July 31, 2026, to RM519.3 million, as well as an almost 10-fold surge in net profit to RM206.3 million.
The operating environment is expected to remain challenging due to ongoing geopolitical tensions, volatility in global supply chains and energy markets as well as rising construction costs, said Crescendo.
However, it is optimistic about the property market outlook in Johor, due to the enhanced cross-border connectivity between Johor Bahru and Singapore through the completion of the Rapid Transit System.
"The current relatively low Overnight Policy Rate has created a favourable environment for housebuyers and investors making homeownership more affordable.
"The government initiatives and steady foreign direct investment inflows into Johor are expected to maintain a healthy demand the industrial properties in the years ahead," it said.
Crescendo will monitor the market situation and implement appropriate measures to mitigate potential impacts on its operations.
"The group will adopt a prudent approach by leveraging on its strategic landbank to develop properties that meet market needs and manage the rising cost," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: From CPR to comfort: The doctor who stayed by Dr Mahathir's side
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: As Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad bade his final farewell to his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, yesterday, three medical personnel stayed close by, watching over the former prime minister.
What caught the public's attention was not just their presence, but the sight of the three — a Malay doctor, an Indian nurse and a Chinese therapist — standing together as they accompanied the 101-year-old former prime minister through one of the most difficult moments of his life.
One of the three was Dr Iskandar Mirza Amran, a Clinical Cardiology Fellow and Specialist in Internal Medicine at the National Heart Institute (IJN).
[[nid:1544092]]
Dr Iskandar, 40, said he was tasked with caring for Dr Mahathir throughout the funeral.
He said there were seven people in IJN's team of seven who treated and supervised Dr Mahathir and his late wife. The team is headed by Datuk Dr Amin Ariff Nuruddin and Datuk Dr Ahmad Khairuddin Mohamed Yusof; and also included Datuk Dr Ghazali Ahmad; Dr Hafidz Abd Hadi; Dr Hisham Md Sharom; Dr Afif Ashaari; and himself.
"Last Sunday, I was on a 24-hour shift. Yesterday morning, we received a 'code blue', which meant an emergency involving Dr Hasmah.
"I was among those called on to perform CPR on her before her passing was confirmed," he said when contacted.
Dr Iskandar said he was then tasked with accompanying Dr Mahathir throughout the burial, as other doctors in the team were attending to another important procedure.
"I saw that Dr Mahathir was grieving. He did not say much, and only wept.
"I checked on him to see if he was experiencing breathing difficulties or chest pains, but he told me he did not have any of those symptoms," he said.
[[nid:1544091]]
On the viral image of him with two other medical personnel - an Indian nurse and a Chinese therapist - Dr Iskandar said he did not think that the image would touch so many Malaysians.
"I can't deny that the public perception of doctors has deteriorated of late due to various factors. That image changed the people's perception.
"Many people contacted me to thank me for taking care of Tun Mahathir. I'm pleased that our presence managed to affect the negative perception towards doctors.
"When I hear the thanks and appreciation from the people, it makes the exhaustion from working for 40 hours worthwhile," he said.
Dr Hasmah, who was 100-years-old, died at the IJN at 9.20am yesterday.
She was buried at the National Cemetery, Presint 20, Putrajaya.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Six escape unhurt after tree falls onto two cars
Article:
IPOH: Six people escaped unhurt after a tree fell onto two cars along Jalan Simpang Pulai-Lahat near Station 18 here today.
Perak Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received a distress call at 4.26pm.
He said a team from the Pasir Puteh Fire and Rescue Station arrived at the scene three minutes later.
"The incident involved a Perodua Bezza and a Perodua Alza. All six occupants managed to get out of the vehicles safely and were not injured," he said.
Sabarodzi said members of the public had assisted the occupants before firefighters arrived.
"Firefighters are carrying out cutting operations to remove the fallen tree," he said.
He added that the operation involved seven firefighters and two vehicles, a Light Fire and Rescue Tender (LFRT) and an Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) vehicle.

Title: Sern Kou winding up plywood business
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sern Kou Resources Bhd will cease the plywood manufacturing operations of its 51 per cent-owned subsidiary Sern Kou Plywood Sdn Bhd, which has been making losses since the financial year 2024.
The timber products manufacturer said the decision was made as there was no reasonable expectation that the subsidiary's financial performance would improve in the foreseeable future.
Sern Kou Plywood recorded revenue of RM12.43 million for the unaudited financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY26), down from RM17.38 million a year earlier.
The subsidiary's revenue contribution to the group also fell to 2.8 per cent in FY26 from 3.57 per cent in FY25, while its share of the group's loss after tax stood at 5.51 per cent.
Following the cessation, Sern Kou Plywood will progressively wind down its operations, including realising inventories, collecting receivables, settling liabilities and contractual commitments, and dealing with its property, plant and equipment.
"The property, plant and equipment may be leased or disposed of based on an internal review, the estimated impairment amounts to approximately RM338,000," it said.
The cessation will affect 88 employees, comprising 14 locals and 74 foreign workers. Some may be retained for winding-down activities, while the remaining employees will be retrenched or transferred within the group where applicable.
The estimated retrenchment cost is RM200,000, subject to final computation.
Based on Sern Kou's 51 per cent equity interest in the unit, the impairment and retrenchment costs are expected to have a financial impact of about RM274,000 on the group.
The company said the cessation will only affect the plywood manufacturing operations and will not impact its other manufacturing businesses, including furniture manufacturing and sawmill operations.
It added that the cessation is not expected to have a material impact on the group's losses or loss per share.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police trace drug ring that recruited five Malaysians held in Jakarta
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracing a drug trafficking syndicate in the country believed to have recruited five Malaysians as drug mules before they were detained by Indonesian authorities in Jakarta last Friday.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspects, four men and a woman aged between 21 and 30, were detained at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport.
He said they were suspected of attempting to smuggle five kilogrammes of synthetic drugs of the etomidate type, concealed in the insoles of their respective shoes.
"An inspection was conducted on the suspects after Indonesian Customs and Excise officers became suspicious of the movements of the five individuals.
"Initial checks found that each of them was carrying two packets of powder suspected to be etomidate, weighing about 500 grammes per packet," he said when contacted today.
Hussein said police had received information from the Directorate of Narcotics Crime (Dittipidnarkoba), Criminal Investigation Agency (Bareskrim), Indonesian National Police (POLRI), regarding the detention of the five Malaysians.
He said the suspects comprised three from Sarawak and two from Pahang, with one having three previous criminal records related to drug offences, while the other four had no previous records.
Hussein said smuggling involving etomidate was a new trend detected by the authorities.
It was previously reported that the
five suspects
were detained shortly after landing in Jakarta on a flight from Kuala Lumpur on Sept 25.
Following the arrests, Indonesian authorities uncovered a secret laboratory producing drug-laced vape liquid at an apartment in North Jakarta.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Haze returns to KL as Cheras, Batu Muda hit unhealthy levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Cheras and Batu Muda recorded unhealthy air quality as of 6pm today, with their Air Pollutant Index (API) readings rising from the morning.
Cheras recorded an API reading of 171, up from 158 at 8.30am, while Batu Muda rose to 157 from 100.
The capital was among 36 areas nationwide recording unhealthy readings,
nine more
than in the morning.
Data from the Air Pollutant Index Management System showed Putrajaya's reading also increased to 166 from 154 at 8.30am.
Johan Setia in Selangor recorded the highest reading nationwide at 177, up from 161 in the morning, followed by Bandaraya Melaka (175), Nilai (174), Shah Alam (173), Serian (173) and Pasir Gudang (173).
Other Klang Valley stations in the unhealthy range were Klang (165), Banting (164), Petaling Jaya (161) and Kuala Selangor (159).
Only five stations recorded good air quality as of 6pm, all in Sabah and Sarawak, with Limbang recording the lowest reading at 26.
Under Malaysia's API classification, readings of 0 to 50 are considered good, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.
Yesterday,
four areas in Johor recorded moderate API readings as of 10am, an improvement from the unhealthy levels recorded the previous day.

Title: Sept 29 designated Malaysian Professionals Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has agreed to designate Sept 29 as Malaysian Professionals Day.
"When it was proposed that Sept 29 be Malaysian Professionals Day, I agreed because it makes sense and serves a purpose," he said.
Anwar was speaking at the inaugural Professionals Conference & Exhibition (Profex 2026) at the KLGCC Convention Centre here today.
He said the professional class was central to national progress, adding that political leaders, civil servants and professionals had to work as one team.
Citing Spanish thinker José Ortega y Gasset, Anwar cautioned that specialisation must not come at the expense of a wider understanding of society, referring to what the thinker called the "barbarism of specialisation".
"Building a city is not only about buildings and concrete.
"If we build only from narrow, specialised viewpoints, we will build a concrete jungle," he said.
Anwar said the pursuit of excellence was also embedded in cultures and faiths familiar to Malaysians, citing the concepts of wasatiyyah (moderation) in Islam, Zhongyong (Doctrine of the Mean) in Confucianism and the "Golden Mean" in the Greek tradition.
The prime minister also warned that professionals could not escape responsibility for governance failures.
"When we look at past scandals, whether 1MDB, Tabung Haji or Felda, the political leadership is responsible, of course. But the professional class is not spared either," he said.
He said many people knew about wrongdoing but remained silent.
"Most people know but cannot speak out. Top professionals know their own field but are deaf and mute about everything else," he said.
Anwar said no country could survive if corruption was tolerated.
Meanwhile, he said he would bring proposals on engaging professionals to the Cabinet and asked Balai Ikhtisas Malaysia's leadership to identify experts in areas such as health, education and information technology.
"Remember, ministers, we do not have expertise in every area. We should listen and evaluate," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Second student arrested over death of Form Two student in Kuala Pilah
Article:
SEREMBAN: Police have arrested another 16-year-old male student to assist in the investigation into the death of a Form Two student in Kuala Pilah last Friday.
This brings the total number of
people arrested in connection with the case
, which is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, to two.
Negri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the latest suspect was a student at the same school and was brought to the Kuala Pilah magistrate's court yesterday for a six-day remand order until Oct 3 to assist investigations.
He also said a special task force had been set up to determine the actual cause of death and investigate whether bullying was involved.
"The post-mortem results are still inconclusive regarding the cause of the victim's death, and police are awaiting the results of samples sent to the Chemistry Department.
"A total of 68 witness statements have been recorded, though several more witnesses will be called to assist investigations," he said at a press conference here today.
Meanwhile, Alzafny said further investigations found that the incident occurred after the Maghrib prayers last Friday, when all students were supposed to be attending a study or "prep" session in their respective dormitories.
He said the suspect then called the victim to his room on the second floor of Block A before beating the victim several times on the soles of his feet with a rubber hose.
"The victim was also struck on several parts of his body. When the victim's condition became critical, the dormitory warden was contacted, and the victim was taken to the hospital. Doctors then confirmed that the victim had died.
"We cannot confirm whether the victim passed away at the dormitory or while on the way to the hospital," he said, adding that several students from the school had also come forward to police, claiming they had previously been bullied by the first suspect detained.
It was previously reported that Alzafny said a Form Four student had been remanded for six days to assist in the investigation into the
death of the 14-year-old Form Two student
in Kuala Pilah.
Alzafny had said police were notified of an incident involving injuries inflicted on a Form Two student at a school in Kuala Pilah, after which the victim was rushed to Tuanku Ampuan Najihah Hospital (HTAN) in Kuala Pilah and confirmed dead.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man assaults motorcyclist after baby's sleep disturbed by loud exhaust
Article:
MERSING: A man is expected to be charged tomorrow with assaulting a motorcyclist at a convenience store in Jalan Ismail here on Friday after allegedly becoming angry over the rider's loud exhaust, which he claimed had woken his baby.
Mersing district police chief Superintendent Abdul Razak Abdullah Sani said police received information about the incident after a 1-minute-45-second video of it went viral on social media.
He said the incident occurred about 1am after the suspect became angry after claiming that the victim had cut in front of his vehicle and revved his motorcycle loudly, causing the baby held by his wife to wake up and cry.
"The suspect then assaulted the victim.
"As a result, the victim sought treatment at hospital and was diagnosed with soft tissue injuries to his left cheek and abdomen," he said in a statement today.
Abdul Razak said police opened an investigation paper and investigated the case under Section 323 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing hurt.
He said the investigation paper had been completed and referred to the Johor deputy public prosecutor today for further action.
"The suspect has been ordered to be charged under Section 323 of the Penal Code and the charge will be made at the Mersing Magistrate's court tomorrow.
"If convicted, the suspect faces up to one year in prison, a maximum fine of RM2,000, or both," he said.
Abdul Razak also advised the public not to act on their emotions, as this could ultimately cause harm to themselves.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Domestic projects will continue to anchor Gamuda's earnings next year
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gamuda Bhd anticipates its earnings performance next year will be predominantly anchored by domestic construction projects, including hyperscale data centre builds, following strong domestic segment performance this year.
The group's earnings visibility remains underpinned by an all-time-high construction orderbook balance of RM61 billion and unbilled property sales of RM7.6 billion, said Gamuda in announcing its earnings for the fourth quarter ended July 31, 2026 (Q4 FY26).
Its net profit rose 5.2 per cent in Q4 FY26 to RM349.7 million, driven mainly by stronger contributions from its domestic construction projects, while revenue jumped 19 per cent year-on-year to RM5.76 billion.
For the full financial year, net profit rose five per cent to RM1.05 billion from RM1 billion, while revenue increased 14 per cent to a record RM18.6 billion from RM15.97 billion.
"The group broke its earnings record for the fifth consecutive year…driven by robust contributions from domestic construction projects and high margin quick-turnaround projects (QTP) in Vietnam," said Gamuda in the filing with Bursa Malaysia.
Domestic projects had become the main growth driver, supported substantially by the data centre segment. Domestic construction earnings surged 49 per cent to RM461 million, while total construction earnings, including overseas projects, rose 19 per cent to RM742 million.
The group said its property division recorded a 14 per cent decline in quarterly revenue and a 41 per cent drop in net profit, mainly due to slower sales conversion across its townships in Malaysia.
Net gearing stood at 72 per cent at end-July 2026, temporarily exceeding the group's self-imposed 70 per cent limit following land acquisitions in Vietnam and Singapore earlier this year to replenish its portfolio of quick-turnaround projects.
"The group's continued ability to generate operating cashflow to fund its capex is evidenced by the near RM800 million surplus cash generated from its operating activities during the year," it said.
Gamuda expects its gearing to decline from next year, supported by cash inflows from its record construction orderbook and RM7.6 billion in unbilled property sales.
This includes the nearly sold-out Eaton Park project in Vietnam, where developers can collect up to 50 per cent of the sales value during construction, with the remaining 50 per cent payable upon handover under Vietnamese law.

Title: Ringgit ends marginally higher against US dollar, S&P Rating supports sentiment
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit strengthened marginally against the US dollar on Tuesday, with market sentiment supported by S&P Global Ratings' reaffirmation of Malaysia's 'A-' sovereign credit rating with a stable outlook.
At 6pm, the ringgit improved to 4.0790/0850 against the greenback from Monday's close of 4.0805/0845.
In a statement today, the Finance Ministry said S&P has reaffirmed Malaysia's 'A-' sovereign credit rating with a stable outlook, citing the economy's resilience and diversification, sustained growth momentum, gradual fiscal consolidation, strong monetary policy flexibility and a historically supportive external position.
The ministry said the stable outlook reflects S&P's expectation that Malaysia's growth momentum and prevailing policy environment will support steady fiscal performance over the next two to three years.
Meanwhile, Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the US dollar remained supported, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) rising 0.19 per cent to 101.391 points.
He said higher US Treasury yields suggested that US Treasury bonds had become more attractive, while expectations of further interest rate hikes by the US Federal Reserve could also make the US dollar more appealing to investors as interest rate differentials continued to favour US dollar-denominated assets.
"Tonight, the main data points will be the US Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index and the US Job Openings and Labour Turnover Survey.
"Judging from the US interest rate futures, the odds are for a total 50 basis point rise for the remainder of 2026 as the inflation rate remains stubbornly above the two per cent target," he told Bernama.
At the closing, the ringgit traded higher against a basket of major currencies.
It increased against the euro to 4.6235/6303 from 4.6416/6461 at Monday's close, climbed vis-à-vis the British pound to 5.3937/4016 from 5.4099/4152, and gained versus the Japanese yen to 2.5869/5909 from 2.5994/6021.
Against Asean currencies, the local note strengthened versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1885/1934 from 3.1914/1948 at yesterday's close, rose against the Indonesian rupiah at 226.8/227.2 from 226.9/227.2, and advanced against the Thai baht to 12.1402/1632 from 12.1429/1588 previously.
However, the local note was flat against the Philippine peso at 6.52/6.53.

Title: Aeon Credit Q2 net profit falls to RM59.3mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Aeon Credit Service (M) Bhd's net profit fell to RM59.3 million in the second quarter (Q2) ended Aug 31, 2026, against RM72.23 million a year ago.
Revenue rose to RM665.19 million from RM617.88 million previously, supported by the stronger loan and financing growth.
For the first half of the financial year ended Feb 28, 2027 (1H FY27), Aeon Credit posted a higher net profit of RM154.46 million versus RM149.77 million previously. Revenue increased to RM1.31 billion compared with RM1.21 billion in the same period a year ago.
In filing with Bursa Malaysia, Aeon Credit said the higher profit for 1H FY27 was driven by higher revenue. This was despite a rise in impairment losses on financing receivables and other higher operating expenses, in line with an increase in transaction and financing volume.
On prospects, the group said it will continue to adopt a cautious and prudent business approach due to heightened geopolitical tensions in the Middle East, which continue to pose risks to global supply chains, elevated global oil prices, associated inflationary pressures and volatility in global financial markets.
"The group remains focused on growing quality financing assets and continues to closely monitor inherent credit risks within its financing portfolio, while enhancing its information technology capabilities.
The group expects to sustain its business momentum by implementing appropriate strategic and operational measures for FY27.
It declared a first interim single-tier dividend of 13 sen per share for FY27, payable on Nov 5, 2026.

Title: Scientex to acquire 70pct interest in China's Mintpack for RM102mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Scientex Bhd, through its wholly-owned subsidiary Scientex Packaging (Ayer Keroh) Bhd (SPAK), has entered into a sale and purchase agreement to acquire a 70 per cent stake in China-based Hunan Changcheng Mint New Material Technology Co., Ltd. (Mintpack).
The proposed acquisition involves a purchase consideration of RMB167.3 million, about RM101.5 million, said Scientex in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday.
The agreement was signed with Tan Cui Fang, and Hunan Changcheng Tianyi Information Technology Co., Ltd. Tan is the founder of both Mintpack and Tianyi.
Upon the completion of the transaction, Mintpack will become an indirect subsidiary of Scientex, while Tianyi will retain the remaining 30 per cent equity interest.
Incorporated in July 2015, Mintpack operates from the Xiangtan Economic and Technological Development Zone in Hunan, China.
The company specialises in the manufacturing of high-quality flexible plastic packaging, including flexible plastic bags and roll films.
Scientex views the acquisition as a strategic avenue to expand the group's consumer packaging footprint into China.
The deal secures the group an established local manufacturing platform and customer base in China, directly complementing Scientex's existing consumer packaging operations.
By leveraging Mintpack's capabilities and market presence, Scientex aims to develop new multinational client relationships and expand its reach into new export markets.
The consolidation of Mintpack's earnings and operations will provide the enlarged Scientex Group with increased production capacity and a diversified portfolio across regional and global markets.
The RM101.5 million purchase consideration was negotiated on a willing-buyer-willing-seller basis. It factors in Mintpack's historical financial performance, its future growth prospects, and its audited net assets of RMB119.5 million as of Dec 31, 2025.
Scientex will finance the acquisition using a combination of internally generated funds and bank borrowings.
The acquisition is not expected to have any material effect on Scientex's earnings per share, net assets per share, gearing, share capital, or substantial shareholders' shareholdings for the financial year ending July 31, 2027.
Barring any unforeseen circumstances and subject to all relevant approvals being obtained, Scientex expects to complete the acquisition of Mintpack by the end of 2026.

Title: Why do so many Malaysians ride motorcycles?
Article:
FOR many riders, the motorcycle is solving a practical problem. It gets them to work affordably, reliably and on time.
The challenge is that the mobility solution millions depend on is also the mode carrying Malaysia's greatest road-safety exposure.
The scale alone tells us motorcycles are not a marginal transport issue. In 2024, 78.1 per cent of Malaysian households owned a motorcycle.
Our preliminary research found more than 13.6 million motorcycle registrations between 2000 and mid-2026, including 655,837 new registrations in 2024.
It has become deeply embedded in Malaysian mobility. But not every motorcyclist is riding for the same reason.
A factory worker travelling before the first bus arrives faces a very different problem from a professional riding into Kuala Lumpur to avoid congestion.
A rural household using a motorcycle to reach a school or clinic has different needs from a university student. A p-hailing rider is different again. For that rider, the motorcycle is not simply transport.
It is the tool that earns the income. Our research identifies industrial and shift workers, delivery riders, congestion-avoidance commuters, rural users, students and early-career workers. Their travel patterns and realistic alternatives differ.
That distinction matters because one policy response cannot work equally well for all of them.
For many workers, the attraction of the motorcycle is easy to understand. Public transport may exist within the wider city, but that does not necessarily mean it connects a person's home to the workplace at the right time.
Our research examined illustrative commuting scenarios involving industrial areas in Klang, Rawang, Senai, Bayan Lepas and Pasir Gudang.
In those examples, public transport journeys could take roughly 50 to 67 minutes longer in one direction than travelling by motorcycle because of indirect routes, transfers, service frequency and weak first- and last-mile connections.
They expose an important issue: people count time spent waiting, walking and changing services.
They consider whether the bus arrives before their shift, whether the last service operates when they finish work, and whether they can reach the final kilometer.
A cheap journey is not necessarily a practical journey if it takes twice as long.
This does not mean motorcycles are always the better mode. It means that, under certain Malaysian conditions, choosing a motorcycle can be an entirely rational decision.
And that is where the national dilemma begins. The safety burden is severe. The research records 6,443 road deaths in 2023, of which 4,489, or 69.4 per cent, involved motorcyclists.
The employment dimension makes this even more serious. PERKESO data examined in the study recorded 46,542 commuting accidents in 2025, representing 50.9 per cent of occupational accident claims in that dataset.
More than 80 per cent of commuting fatalities recorded there involved motorcyclists.
When the journey to work becomes one of the most dangerous parts of the working day, motorcycle safety is no longer only a traffic issue. It becomes a workforce issue.
[[nid:1543981]]
That does not mean rider behaviour should be ignored. Speeding matters. Helmets matter. Licensing, vehicle condition and enforcement matter.
But so do road design, traffic speeds, public transport accessibility, working hours and the amount of time riders are exposed to traffic.
The objective should not be to replace rider-blaming with system-blaming, but to understand the whole system.
Malaysia already has useful experience. The country pioneered dedicated motorcycle facilities on corridors such as the Federal Highway and KESAS.
Research cited in our study found meaningful safety gains from segregation, while also identifying weaknesses involving road geometry, barriers, drainage, lighting and the places where motorcycle lanes reconnect with mixed traffic.
The lesson is not simply to build more motorcycle lanes. The better question is where separation works, how it should be designed, and how the entire journey can be made safer.
Motorcycles and public transport should not always be treated as competitors. Some motorcycle trips could shift entirely to buses or rail. Others may be shortened.
Could we make it easier for someone to ride three kilometres to a station instead of 30 kilometres to work?
Our research raises this possibility through better motorcycle-to-transit integration, including secure parking and safer access to stations.
Other journeys will remain motorcycle-dependent, especially for commercial riders and people living or working in places with limited alternatives. Those journeys must be made substantially safer.
This is why MYARTTE (MY Asean Road and Traffic Tech Expo) intends to convene a Roundtable on Motorcycle Mobility in Malaysia.
The purpose is not to begin with a predetermined solution or assign blame. It is to bring government agencies, researchers, industry, employers, operators and riders together around three basic questions.
Why are Malaysians riding? Which motorcycle journeys could realistically be replaced or shortened? How do we make the journeys that remain much safer?
No single agency controls all the factors involved. Transport planning, road engineering, enforcement, vehicle standards, public transport, urban development, employment and social protection all influence the outcome.
For many Malaysians, the motorcycle is not the problem. It is the answer to a problem: how to reach work, education and opportunity at a price and within a time they can afford.
The challenge for Malaysia is to provide better answers. We should continue asking how motorcyclists can ride more safely.
But if we are serious about reducing the human cost, we must also ask why so many Malaysians have to ride in the first place.
* The writer is founder & senior adviser, My Mobility Vision
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Missing Orang Asli woman found dead in Rompin swamp
Article:
ROMPIN: The search for a missing 73-year-old Orang Asli woman ended today when her body was found in a swampy area in Kampung Lesung, Kedaik, police said.
The remains of Kuang Poh,
who was last seen
leaving her home for a fishing trip on Sept 22, were found at 11.50am.
Rompin district police chief Superintendent Sharif Shai Sharif Mondoi said search and rescue (SAR) team members found Kuang's decomposed remains about 500 metres from where she was last seen.
"SAR teams today focused on several areas within a five-kilometre radius of the settlement before her remains were spotted in an overgrown swampy area.
"The remains were taken to Rompin Hospital for a post-mortem examination at 1.05pm. The case has been classified as sudden death," he said in a statement today.
Kuang failed to return home after leaving for a fishing trip at about 3pm on Sept 22, prompting a relative to lodge a missing person report the following day.
Yesterday, Sharif Shai said the swampy terrain and the risk of
encountering wild animals
, including leopards, tigers and elephants, were among the challenges faced by SAR teams.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: After Finance Ministry says no duty due on K8 cargo, Maritime Network asks Customs dept to put ruling on record
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Maritime Network Sdn Bhd is seeking a written explanation from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (JKDM) following a meeting with the Ministry of Finance (MOF) over the handling of Atlanta crude discharged at Tanjung Langsat under a K8 declaration.
At the September 25 discussion, chaired by MOF Tax Division Under-Secretary Datuk John Patrick Antonysamy and attended by JKDM officers, the chair said no duty was due on the cargo as presented.
He also raised a separate question for Customs: how the K8 cargo was transferred to another party
Maritime Network said both points need to be recorded and explained in writing before the company can close its compliance file.
“If MOF’s position is that no duty is payable, we are asking for the provisions, exemptions and factual assumptions behind that conclusion. We will respect a reasoned answer.
“But a verbal conclusion cannot tell a shipping agent which documents supported a cargo transfer, what declaration closed the movement, or why the agent was compounded,” said Maritime Network managing director Datuk Seri R. Jeyenderan.
The meeting focused principally on approximately 42,051 tonnes associated with MT Invictus. Maritime has also separately raised questions about another Atlanta crude cargo carried by MT Marlin Santorini.
The two cargoes had a combined declared value of more than RM220 million. That figure represents their declared cargo value, not an estimate of unpaid tax.
Maritime Network said a K8 document discussed at the meeting was interpreted differently by those present.
Its representatives questioned whether an outward record continued to describe Atlanta crude despite reported blending into very low sulphur fuel oil, while an officer described the document shown as an inward movement between Customs stations.
Maritime  Network is asking JKDM to resolve the issue using the full set of certified declarations, warehouse records and final movement documents. It is not asserting that a false outward declaration has been established.
The company is also requesting a separate review of a compound it says was imposed over manifest documentation.
It wants JKDM to state the precise alleged omission, why responsibility was assigned to Maritime, and what review route is available. MOF’s verbal conclusion on duty did not itself cancel the compound.
MIDA, in a written response dated September 17, said questions concerning activity at a Public Licensed Warehouse and applicable duties should be directed to JKDM.
Maritime Network said it is now seeking a coordinated written answer from MOF and Customs identifying the applicable legal instruments, any approvals or exemptions, and the records supporting their conclusions.
“This is not a request to declare somebody guilty. It is a request to show the governing rule and the transaction trail,” Jeyenderan said.
“If the process was permitted and no tax was due, put that reasoning on record. If a declaration needs correcting, say what should be corrected and by whom. Everyone in the industry needs an answer they can actually follow.”
Maritime  Network said it would consider and fairly reflect any substantive written response from MOF or JKDM. It has not received an official written determination on the points discussed at the meeting as at the time of this draft.

Title: Sarawak vaccinates 3,579 dogs, distributes 2,281 oral rabies vaccine baits in latest drive
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 29 — A total of 3,579 dogs have been vaccinated through Sarawak’s recent field rabies vaccination efforts this year, alongside the distribution of 2,281 oral rabies vaccine (ORV) baits, said Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
He said the ORV programme provided an important last-mile approach to reaching free-roaming dogs that were difficult to capture and vaccinate through conventional methods.
“The programme provides an important last-mile approach for reaching free-roaming dogs that are difficult to capture and vaccinate through conventional parenteral vaccination,” he said in a speech read by Deputy Premier Datuk Amar Dr Sim Kui Hian during the Rabies in Asia (RIA) 2026 conference in conjunction with Rabies in Borneo (RIB) 2026 at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK) here.
Abang Johari said Sarawak continued to strengthen its rabies prevention and control measures through vaccination, surveillance, enforcement, public awareness and collaboration with its partners.
The efforts involve the Department of Veterinary Services Sarawak, Immune Belt Enforcement Team (IBET), Sarawak Infectious Disease Centre (SIDC), Sarawak Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (SSPCA), local authorities and other partners.
The programme is also supported by international organisations including Mission Rabies and Ceva Santé Animale.
“This demonstrates that tackling rabies requires more than government intervention alone.
“It requires technical expertise, field experience, community participation and the willingness of different organisations to work together towards a common goal.
“The same principle applies to our efforts across borders,” said Abang Johari. — The Borneo Post

Title: Home minister: Government resolving persistent refugee problem according to rule of law
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Madani Government will not allow the problem of foreign refugee presence to persist indefinitely; instead, it has begun resolving the issue firmly, systematically, and in stages based on the Constitution and the rule of law, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
He said that a total of 5,000 Myanmar refugees have been finalised to undergo a voluntary and phased repatriation programme back to their country of origin, based on the Myanmar government’s agreement to accept them and the individuals’ consent to return voluntarily.
“Today, a total of 1,476 individuals began the First Phase of repatriation, based on the list submitted by the Myanmar Government through an official Diplomatic Note.
“This implementation is coordinated by the Ministry of Home Affairs together with the Malaysian Immigration Department and related agencies. This resolution was also achieved through diplomatic approaches and direct negotiations with the Myanmar Government,” he said in a statement today.
Saifuddin Nasution noted that the presence of foreign refugees, particularly from Myanmar, has dragged on for decades without a definitive resolution, turning into a massive financial burden for the country, triggering serious social crises, and posing a tangible security threat to the citizens.
He said that for issues involving two countries, enforcement actions alone are insufficient; instead, they require cooperation from the country of origin to enable the acceptance, documentation, and repatriation processes to be carried out in an orderly and phased manner.
“This is the approach we are taking: the law is upheld, enforcement is implemented, and diplomatic channels are utilised to produce a solution.
“Although Malaysia is not a State Party to the 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees and its 1967 Protocol, we choose a firm yet civilised approach centered on the values of compassion and the spirit of ASEAN familyhood, with every action executed in an orderly and responsible manner without compromising national security and sovereignty,” he said.
Saifuddin Nasution stated that today’s first phase was just a beginning, while subsequent phases will proceed as soon as the identification, documentation, verification, and operational readiness processes are completed.
“We are beginning to resolve a legacy problem that has dragged on for a long time, based on the law. We safeguard national sovereignty. The security, welfare, and interests of Malaysian citizens remain the top priority.”
A total of 1,476 Myanmar refugee detainees - comprising 1,370 men, 79 women, and 27 children - were repatriated at the Royal Malaysian Navy (RMN) Base in Lumut, Perak, today.
The repatriation process was carried out using Myanmar Navy ships, namely the UMS Moattama, escort vessel UMS King Sin Phyu Shin, and medical ship UMS Thanlwin. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB seen leaving palace after nearly three-hour audience with Tuanku Muhriz
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 29 —Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim concluded an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Hinggap here after spending nearly three hours at the palace.

Earlier, vehicles carrying Undang Luak Sungai Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari and Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid were also seen entering the palace grounds.
The meeting is understood to be related to the state’s administration and the ongoing situation in Negeri Sembilan.
