The affected Exco members are Datuk Mohd Faizal Ramli, Datuk Zaifulbahri Idris, Datuk Mustapha Nagoor, Siow Kong Choon, Siti Nur Umaira Hasim, Datuk Mohd Asna Amin, Datuk Mohd Razi Mohd Ali, Suhaimizan Bizar, Mohd Fairuz Mohd Isa and Datuk Razali Abu Samah. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar: Malaysian government to continue talks with Myanmar on refugee status
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Malaysian government will continue engaging with Myanmar to find an amicable solution to the long-standing issue of refugees.
He said the issue, which has remained unresolved for decades, had become more complicated as the number of refugees increased, including through negotiations on their possible return.
“That is why in our negotiations, we tie all these together.
“It is easy for them to say: ‘Don’t send them back.’ Where are we going to put these hundreds of thousands?
“So now what we want are conditions so that there is safety. That is why we invited them to negotiate,” he told reporters when met after launching the Professional Conference and Exhibition 2026 (PROFEX 2026) in conjunction with the Malaysia Professional Day.
He said without resolve and negotiations, it may lead to protests.
Anwar, in expressing appreciation that the Myanmar President had accepted the invitation, has said to allow the matter to be discussed and negotiated.
“So I’m glad that the President is kind enough to accept the invitation and we use that opportunity to discuss, negotiate and even when they agreed to bring back some of these refugees, of course we have to make sure they’ll be protected and whatever facilities be accorded.
“But just to say don’t send them back… There are a lot of concerns here too.
“No country can just accept hundreds of thousands and some countries millions. You have to be able to negotiate,” he added.
He said that the Malaysian government’s position is to protect the refugees’ welfare, human rights concerns.
“But to just condemn us for taking this initiative, I don’t think it’s fair.
“We are trying to find an amicable resolution to this issue.
“That is why I’ve invited him to continue to negotiate and see the parameters… how to resolve this.”
Further commenting, Anwar said, so far the ones sent, they will bring back their people.
“What else can we do? At least we take the trouble.
“Just push them back? No, it’s not true to say just push them back.
“We will first negotiate,” he said.
Anwar said the decision to invite the Myanmar President was important.
“They’ve been there. It’s not a perfect system.
“Some people say that ours is not perfect system too. Many countries are not perfect but still being recognised.”
“I’ve always said there’s the hypocrisy, as many of the countries in the West have been shouting against us but they can accept the atrocities by the Israeli government.
“And when it comes to here, we are trying to resolve,” he said.
The Prime Minister stressed that Malaysia was stringent in its conditions.
“What is the solution?
“As being suggested by many of this organisations, keep them here? How many hundred thousands? Two hundred thousand?
“We use this platform diplomatically to negotiate,” he said.

Title: PM Anwar: Professional expertise must go beyond specialisation to bring Malaysia forward
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today called on Malaysia’s professional community to move beyond narrow specialisation and work across disciplines.
He said expertise alone was insufficient to drive the country’s progress.
“Professionals needed to integrate their specialised knowledge with a broader understanding of society, culture and the country’s needs, rather than working in isolation.
“What is great about professional life is that it brings together people from different disciplines, different races and different regions,” he said when launching the Professional Conference and Exhibition 2026 (PROFEX 2026) in conjunction with the Malaysia Professional Day.
Anwar added that professionals should not view one another through the lens of race, religion or region, but instead build stronger common ground around what was right, just and fair.
He said this was particularly important as Malaysia navigated rapid technological and economic changes, with new areas of expertise emerging in fields such as computing and digital transformation.
The Prime Minister stressed that specialisation should be accompanied by integration, including an understanding of one’s responsibilities towards family, society and the wider world.
He also urged professionals not to remain silent when confronted with dishonesty, corruption and abuses, saying professional responsibility extended beyond technical expertise.
“No country can ever survive in a system that allows cheating, corruption and excesses, and a lack of professionalism,” he said.
Anwar said professionals therefore have a responsibility to contribute towards strengthening governance and ensuring that systems served the country and its people.
“Malaysia’s future depended on professionals who could work together despite differences in culture and religion, while maintaining a strong commitment to justice and fairness.
“This is a national issue. It is relevant to all of us, and professionals in particular have a responsibility to ensure that this nation succeeds.
“And this nation succeeds through unity, through understanding gaps, respect — respect for our differences, cultural and religious — but more importantly, we need a strong sense of commitment to what is right, what is just and what is fair,” he said.
Anwar’s remarks come a day after he similarly called for technological advancement, including artificial intelligence and digital transformation, to remain grounded in ethics, culture and societal values.
Speaking at the International Future Conference 2026 in Kuala Lumpur yesterday, he said discussions about the future should not be confined to algorithms, computing power or economic outcomes, but should also incorporate philosophy, history and moral considerations.
PROFEX 2026, held under the theme “Uniting Professions, Transforming Malaysia’s Future”, brings together professionals, industry leaders, academia, government agencies and emerging talent, with an emphasis on interdisciplinary collaboration, knowledge exchange and professional development.

Title: PM Anwar says will ‘discuss’ transport minister’s plan to resign
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has said today he will discuss Anthony Loke’s decision step down as Transport Minister.
This comes after the Prime Minister receiving Loke’s letter of resignation yesterday.
“Anthony Loke, he just submitted his letter yesterday, I was rushing to Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s funeral.
“What’s the problem? His work has been good, his performance as a minister is also good.
“So I will discuss this,” Anwar said when my by reporters after launching the Malaysia Professional Day’s inaugural conference.
Earlier today, Loke said he will stay on as transport minister until former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak begins his house arrest.
This was a timeframe agreed with the Prime Minister, until a decision is finalised.
Loke had explained that his resignation is a party decision, conveying the DAP’s disagreement with the conditional pardon that allows Najib to serve the remainder of this prison term at home.
Earlier this month, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, consented to granting a conditional pardon to Najib, allowing him to serve the remainder of his jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
This pardon is subject to Najib settling a RM50 million fine.
Najib has been serving a 12-year jail term at Kajang Prison following his conviction in the SRC International case in August 2022.
Previously in 2024, the Pardons Board had already halved his sentence to six years and reduced his fine from RM210 million to RM50 million.

Title: UN concerned by Malaysia returns of Myanmar migrants
Article:
GENEVA, Sept 29 — The UN voiced worry today as Malaysia started sending thousands of Myanmar nationals back to the war-torn country, warning that conditions there would not enable “safe, dignified and sustainable returns”.
Malaysia began repatriating around 1,500 Myanmar nationals today, launching the first phase of a return programme that has raised concerns from rights groups.
The group is the first of 5,000 Myanmar nationals that Malaysia says have agreed to “voluntary” repatriation from detention centres.
“We are concerned,” United Nations refugee agency spokesman Matthew Saltmarsh told reporters in Geneva.
“With ongoing armed conflict and widespread violence and human rights violations across Myanmar, UNHCR maintains that current conditions do not permit safe, dignified and sustainable returns,” he said.
Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced in July that Myanmar had agreed to take back 5,000 members of its persecuted Rohingya minority, in a rare repatriation push that has prompted concern from rights groups.
Myanmar earlier this month pledged “safe and dignified” returns for its citizens displaced abroad, after criticism from the UN and rights groups.
It was not immediately clear on Tuesday how many in the first group en route to Myanmar were Rohingya, and Malaysian authorities did not divulge the number.
But the Muslim minority makes up two-thirds of the 190,000 Myanmar refugees and asylum seekers in the country, according to the UN.
“Under international law, no one should be sent to a country where they may face persecution, torture, serious harm or other threats to life, liberty and security,” Saltmarsh insisted. — AFP

Title: Heavy rain, gusty winds expected across peninsula and Sarawak until 7pm, warns MetMalaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a thunderstorm warning for several states in Peninsular Malaysia and Sarawak, with thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds expected until 7pm today.
In Peninsular Malaysia, the warning covers Penang, Perak and Melaka, as well as parts of five other states.
In Kedah, the affected districts are Pokok Sena, Kota Setar, Padang Terap, Pendang, Yan, Kuala Muda, Kulim, Bandar Baharu, Sik and Baling. In Pahang, they are Bera, Rompin, Kuantan, Maran and Jerantut.
In Selangor, Klang and Kuala Langat are affected, while in Negeri Sembilan the warning covers Tampin and Jempol. In Johor, the districts are Segamat, Tangkak, Muar, Pontian and Batu Pahat.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Sri Aman, Betong, Sarikei (Sarikei and Maradong), Sibu (Sibu), Samarahan (Sebuyau) and Kapit (Song).
MetMalaysia said a warning is issued when there are signs that thunderstorms with rainfall intensity exceeding 20mm per hour are imminent, or are expected to last for more than an hour.
A thunderstorm warning is a short-term alert and is valid for no more than six hours for each issuance, the department said.

Title: Women’s ministry: Victims of sexual harassment need to speak up, no shame in it
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Sept 29 —The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is calling on students to know their boundaries, dare to say no, and seek help if they face sexual harassment or violence.
Deputy Minister Lim Hui Ying said this awareness is crucial to keeping schools a safe environment for children.
Beyond victims coming forward, she said, friends and family members must also play their part by offering support if they notice behavioural changes or suspicious circumstances among those close to them.
“If they feel they cannot accept it, they must dare to say no. We also want to teach them how to seek help when someone faces sexual harassment or violence.
“This is not a case or situation to be ashamed of. They must dare to come forward and look for channels of help,” she told reporters after the Zero Tolerance for Violence: Respect the Boundaries programme at Sekolah Menengah Jenis Kebangsaan Chung Ling here today.
Lim said bullying, sexual harassment and violence require a cross-ministry approach, covering advocacy, prevention, awareness and counselling.
She said KPWKM, through the Social Welfare Department, also has professional counsellors who can assist schools if needed.
Meanwhile, Lim said 142 complaints had been filed with the Tribunal for Anti-Sexual Harassment (TAGS) as of Sept 20, with 97 of them successfully resolved.
She said TAGS, established under the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act 2022, gives individuals facing sexual harassment an alternative avenue to seek easier, quicker and more affordable resolutions.
Lim said the rise in sexual harassment cases reported to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) should also be viewed in terms of greater awareness and more individuals having the courage to come forward for help.
Based on PDRM statistics, 477 sexual harassment cases were recorded in 2022, rising to 522 in 2023, 788 in 2024 and 1,038 in 2025, while 388 cases were reported as of May 31 this year. — Bernama

Title: Woman found unconscious behind a building in Sabah dies
Article:
PENAMPANG, Sept 29 — A 38-year-old local woman died after she was found unconscious on the ground behind a building in Donggongon here yesterday.
Penampang police chief Supt Sammy Newton said police received a report on the incident at about 12.36pm.
“Initial investigations found that the woman was believed to have fallen from the fifth floor of the building.
“She sustained serious injuries and died while being taken to Queen Elizabeth Hospital I in Kota Kinabalu at about 1.05pm,” he said in a statement.
Sammy said the cause of the incident is still under investigation, and the case has been classified as sudden death (SDR). A post-mortem will be conducted to determine the actual cause of death.
Those with information are urged to contact the investigating officer, Penampang police station chief Insp Ahmad Amir Fitri Ab Rahman at 016-449 2215.
The public has also been advised against speculation or sharing photographs and videos of the incident out of respect for the victim’s family and privacy. — The Borneo Post

Title: Home Ministry: 1,476 Myanmar nationals leave Malaysia in first ‘voluntary’ repatriation phase
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — A total of 1,476 Myanmar nationals departed Malaysia today under the first phase of a “voluntary” repatriation programme aimed at resolving a protracted, decades-long refugee and undocumented migrant challenge, the Home Ministry (KDN) announced.
The operation is being conducted by sea via two naval vessels and a hospital ship deployed by the Myanmar government, coordinated jointly by KDN, the Immigration Department of Malaysia (JIM), and relevant security agencies.
Amid ongoing scrutiny from human rights and refugee advocacy groups, the ministry reiterated that the repatriation is being executed on a phased and consensual basis, following formal verification and a bilateral agreement with Naypyidaw to accept the returnees.
KDN stated that as of Aug 15, a total of 10,388 Myanmar nationals held across Immigration detention depots nationwide have been undergoing biometric identification, immigration status assessments, and security screenings.
“Of that number, 5,000 Myanmar nationals have been finalised to undergo a voluntary and phased repatriation programme to their country of origin, based on the Myanmar government’s agreement to receive them and the consent of the individuals involved to return voluntarily,” the ministry said in a statement today.
The initial cohort of 1,476 individuals was selected from a verified list submitted by the Myanmar government through an official diplomatic note.
A decades-long policy challenge
KDN stressed that the prolonged presence of displaced foreign nationals, with Myanmar nationals accounting for more than 95 per cent of all registered refugees in the country, has persisted for decades without a sustainable resolution.
The ministry noted that the situation has imposed substantial financial burdens on public infrastructure, created socio-economic friction, and posed long-term national security concerns for Malaysians.
It said that the MADANI administration is enforcing a phased, structured approach grounded in the Federal Constitution and the rule of law.
“Although Malaysia is not a state party to the 1951 Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees and its 1967 Protocol, the approach taken remains rooted in the value of compassion and the Asean spirit of kinship, ensuring that actions are carried out in an orderly, responsible and humane manner without compromising national security and sovereignty,” the statement read.
The ministry added that ongoing bilateral diplomacy alongside rigorous domestic enforcement enables the government to establish comprehensive profiling and biometric data for foreign nationals residing in the country.
KDN confirmed that subsequent repatriation phases will be carried out progressively, subject to document verification, logistical coordination, and operational readiness between Malaysian and Myanmar authorities.

Title: DVS tests 18 dogs following rabies scare in Kedah’s Changlun
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — The Kedah Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) has collected samples from 18 dogs in Changlun, Kedah, and surrounding areas for rabies confirmatory testing as of yesterday, following an incident where a man was bitten by a stray dog in the area.
In a statement today, DVS announced that the case involving the 31-year-old man was reported by the Kedah State Health Department on Sept 24.
Subsequently, Kedah DVS conducted an on-site investigation and carried out operations to capture stray dogs in collaboration with the Kubang Pasu Municipal Council to locate the suspected animal and assess the potential presence of the rabies virus.
“As of Sept 28, samples have been collected from 18 dogs in the vicinity of the bite incident for rabies confirmatory testing. Kedah DVS is continuing its investigation and awaiting laboratory results to confirm the presence of rabies among dogs in Kedah,” the statement read.
DVS noted that Changlun is located within the rabies buffer zone or immune belt which extends 50 kilometres from the Thai border.
“In this area, all owned dogs are required to undergo rabies vaccination under the Animals Act 1953. This measure is implemented to reduce the risk of rabies spreading to other areas. As of August this year, 504 owned dogs in the Kubang Pasu district, and 1,349 owned dogs across Kedah, have received the rabies vaccine,” the statement added.
Meanwhile, Kedah DVS is continuing its rabies surveillance programme across all districts; 164 samples were tested as of August, all of which returned negative results.
Monitoring and sampling activities have also been intensified in areas bordering Thailand to ensure there is no spread of the rabies outbreak into the country.
Rabies affects the nervous system and can be fatal. Infected dogs may exhibit behavioral changes such as becoming aggressive or unusually docile, restless, or withdrawn and may bark or bite without provocation.
Other symptoms include weakness, loss of coordination, difficulty swallowing, excessive salivation, and paralysis, eventually leading to death.
In this regard, DVS advises the public not to approach, touch, or handle stray or abandoned dogs, sick dogs, or any animals displaying unusual behaviour.
DVS further advises individuals bitten or scratched by a dog or other animal suspected of carrying rabies to wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and to seek immediate medical treatment at a health facility, even if the wound appears minor.
“Report any biting incidents to the nearest Veterinary Services Office to enable investigations and follow-up actions to be carried out while also ensuring owned dogs receive rabies vaccinations in accordance with DVS directives and are not allowed to roam freely,” the statement read.
Kedah DVS will continue to collaborate with the Kedah State Health Department, local authorities, and relevant agencies on monitoring, investigations, and the implementation of control measures to safeguard both animal and public health.
Members of the public in Kedah can provide information or lodge reports with the Field Operations Centre at the Kubang Pasu District Veterinary Services Office by calling 04-916 2207, or with the State Operations Centre at 04-702 5336.
Those outside Kedah may submit reports to their nearest Veterinary Services Office or contact the DVS hotline at 03-8870 2041. — Bernama

Title: MACC: Ex-senior exec to be charged over RM42m UiTM Holdings loss
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — A former senior executive of a corporation will be charged in court this Thursday in connection with the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into losses incurred by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd, including allegations of abuse of power regarding operational expense payments to several companies totalling about RM42 million.
In a statement, MACC announced that the male suspect in his 50s, was arrested at around 1 pm yesterday at his residence in the Klang Valley.
Preliminary investigations revealed that the suspect allegedly committed the act in 2017 by authorising operational expense payments to several companies in which he is believed to have held an interest.
“The arrest follows an investigation conducted by MACC regarding issues concerning losses suffered by UiTM Holdings Sdn Bhd (UiTM Holdings) in 2023,” the statement read.
Meanwhile, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman confirmed the arrest when contacted and stated that the case is being investigated under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: Guan Eng says foreign workers should be excluded from minimum wage hike, calls for EPF levy repeal
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Sept 29 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng today called on the government to exclude foreign workers from any increase in Malaysia’s minimum wage, arguing that the move would help protect local businesses, particularly micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), from rising operating costs.
In a statement, Lim said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to announce a revision to the minimum wage during the tabling of Budget 2027 on Oct 9, following the government’s assessment that wage growth has not kept pace with gains in worker productivity and corporate profits.
While acknowledging the rationale for higher wages, Lim said the prospect of a minimum wage increase has sparked concern among local businesses already grappling with intense competition, higher compliance costs and taxes, as well as price pressures from overseas producers.
He said MSMEs, which form the backbone of the domestic economy, are facing mounting challenges amid a sluggish economic environment and should be consulted before any policy changes are implemented.
Lim argued that any upward revision in the minimum wage should apply only to Malaysian workers, saying foreign employees should not benefit from the increase as they were hired under mutually agreed employment contracts.
He also renewed calls for the immediate abolition of the mandatory two per cent Employees Provident Fund (EPF) contribution for foreign workers, contending that the requirement imposes an unnecessary burden on employers without providing meaningful benefits to migrant workers.
According to Lim, exempting foreign workers from minimum wage increases and scrapping the EPF contribution requirement would help ease cost pressures on local businesses and safeguard the viability of approximately 1.2 million MSMEs nationwide.
He urged the government to prioritise the interests of domestic enterprises and ensure that policies designed to raise wages do not inadvertently undermine the competitiveness of Malaysian businesses.

Title: Public to get live access to Sabah 40pc revenue appeal at Kota Kinabalu court
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 29 — Up to 250 members of the public will be able to follow the Court of Appeal hearing on Sabah’s constitutional 40 per cent revenue entitlement next month through a live audiovisual transmission at the Kota Kinabalu Court Complex.
The arrangement will allow members of the public to watch the proceedings from the court’s conference hall while the appeal is heard inside the courtroom on Oct 29.
The proceedings will not be broadcast online to the wider public, but the arrangement will allow members of the public to follow the hearing in real time from within the court premises.
The Court of Appeal is scheduled to hear the federal government’s appeal against the High Court’s October 17, 2025 decision in the judicial review brought by the Sabah Law Society (SLS).
Former SLS president Datuk Roger Chin, who is now a nominated assemblyman, said the public access arrangement provided an opportunity for Sabahans to witness the proceedings concerning what he described as a significant constitutional issue.
“This is not an online broadcast of the proceedings to the wider world, but something more immediate and meaningful for the people of Sabah — an opportunity to attend the Court Complex, sit within the premises of the Court and follow the hearing in real time,” he said in a statement today.
The appeal concerns, among other matters, the High Court’s findings and orders relating to Sabah’s constitutional entitlement for the period from 1974 to 2021.
The High Court had ruled that the Federal Government had failed to properly conduct the periodic review of Sabah’s special grant under Articles 112C and 112D of the Federal Constitution.
It ordered the federal and Sabah governments to conduct a review of the entitlement for each financial year from 1974 to 2021 and to reach an agreement on the matter.
The federal government subsequently appealed, and the Court of Appeal in April granted a stay of execution of the High Court’s order pending disposal of the appeal. The stay preserved the position pending the appeal and did not determine the substantive constitutional questions.
Under Articles 112C and 112D of the Federal Constitution, Sabah is entitled to a special grant calculated according to a constitutional formula and subject to periodic review.
The SLS has maintained that the failure to conduct the required reviews between 1974 and 2021 was unlawful, while the federal government’s position is that the fixed grant under the earlier review order remained legally effective until it was superseded by a new order in 2022.
The competing positions will now be considered by the Court of Appeal.
Chin said the public viewing arrangement would provide wider access to a hearing which previously could only accommodate a limited number of people inside the courtroom.
He said the initiative should be viewed as an opportunity for the public to understand the legal arguments rather than as an attempt to influence the court.
“The purpose of attending is not to prejudge the appeal, exert pressure upon the Court or influence its decision, but to allow an informed, peaceful and engaged people to bear witness to a constitutional question that belongs to all Sabahans,” he said.
The appeal is scheduled to begin at 9am on Thursday, October 29, at the Kota Kinabalu Court Complex.
Members of the public attending the viewing will be subject to the capacity of the conference hall, security requirements and directions issued by the court and court administration.
Chin encouraged those intending to attend to arrive early to allow sufficient time for security procedures.
“History should not be watched from afar. On Oct 29, let Sabah be present — and let Sabah be seen to care,” he said.

Title: Marina Mahathir: My father healthy but lonely after loss of beloved wife
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad is coping with a deep sense of loneliness following the death of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohd Ali, whom he shared more than seven decades of marriage with, according to their daughter, Datuk Marina Mahathir.
Berita Harian
reported that Marina said her 101-year-old father remains in good health but is grieving the loss of his lifelong companion, who died yesterday at the age of 100.
“Of course he is sad. She was his partner for 70 years. He feels lonely,” Marina told reporters after visiting Dr Hasmah’s grave at Pusara Negara in Presint 20 today.
She said family members have been taking turns to stay with Dr Mahathir around the clock to ensure he is not left alone during this difficult period.
“He feels very alone now. How could he not be sad? She was his partner for 70 years,” she said.
Marina added that the loss has been felt by the entire family, who are still coming to terms with Siti Hasmah’s absence after years of having her at the centre of family life.
“We all miss mother. We were so used to seeing her at home, and now it is hard to believe she is no longer with us,” she said.
Dr Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute yesterday morning. Her death was confirmed by her son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir.
Marina also thanked members of the public who paid their respects at the mosque and later at the burial grounds, saying the family had been touched by the overwhelming show of affection and support.
She said hundreds of condolence messages had poured in through WhatsApp and other channels, making it impossible to respond to each one personally.
According to Marina, many Malaysians regarded Siti Hasmah as a mother figure, making the tributes especially meaningful for the family.
Asked about visits to Dr Mahathir, Marina said her father remains open to receiving well-wishers, although the number of visitors would need to be managed to avoid overwhelming him.
“Father can receive visitors, but we have to control the numbers. There cannot be too many at one time,” she said.

Title: Dr M recalls shock at wife Dr Hasmah’s sudden passing despite signs of good health
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Sept 29 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad has said he did not expect his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Ali, to pass away yesterday, recalling that she had appeared to be in good health the night before.
Speaking during a visit by the Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Sultan Ahmad Shah, who came to pay his last respects, Dr Mahathir shared his surprise at the sudden loss in a video posted online.
“I didn’t expect her to die today,” he said, adding that Hasmah had seemed “quite well” the previous evening.
The Pahang ruler was accompanied by Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah and Tengku Mahkota Pahang Tengku Hassanal Ibrahim Alam Shah during the condolence visit. Dr Mahathir also thanked the royal family for making the journey from Pahang to offer their condolences.
Dr Hasmah died at about 9.25am yesterday at the National Heart Institute. She was 100 years old.
She was accorded a state funeral before being laid to rest at Pusara Negara in Putrajaya on the same day. Her passing prompted an outpouring of tributes from leaders and members of the public, many remembering her warmth, grace and contributions to the nation.
Her son, Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir, said Dr Hasmah had been in good spirits the night before her death, but her condition deteriorated suddenly the following day. Another son, Datuk Seri Mukhriz Mahathir, said Dr Mahathir remained by her side until her final moments.
Dr Mahathir and Dr Hasmah were married for 70 years, forming one of Malaysia’s most enduring and recognisable partnerships in public life.

Title: Nanta: New Johor Bahru court complex among 11 judicial projects worth RM736m nationwide
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Sept 29 — The new Johor Bahru court complex in Kota Iskandar is among 11 judicial infrastructure projects being developed nationwide with a cumulative value of RM736 million, Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said today.
Nanta said that other judicial complexes nearing completion under the national programme include facilities in Temerloh, Pahang; Sri Aman, Sarawak; and Ipoh, Perak.
“The Johor Bahru court complex project was approved by the Economic Planning Unit (EPU) of the Prime Minister's Department back in 2018 under the 11th Malaysia Plan.
“The project was executed using a design-and-build approach with an approved cost of RM200 million," he said during the official project handover ceremony here today.
Also present at the event was Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Nanta said construction began on February 8, 2023, and was successfully concluded within its approved schedule and budget.
The building's architectural concept integrates traditional Malay and vernacular design philosophies, drawing directly from Johor’s cultural heritage.
“This is reflected in the facade and interior décor through the application of
gambir
and black pepper motifs, as well as intricate
kerawang
elements that is synonymous with the state's identity,” he said.
Spanning 6.88 hectares within the state administrative centre of Kota Iskandar, the complex houses 24 courtrooms: one Special Court, seven High Courts, eight Sessions Courts, and eight Magistrates' Courts.
The facility is also equipped with modern judicial amenities, including judges' chambers, administrative and finance suites, an auditorium, a legal library, and secure segregated holding cells and transit corridors for detainees.
The complex is scheduled to become fully operational by early next year.
Meanwhile, Azalina said the vacated Johor Bahru court complex in the city centre will be formally returned to the Johor state government.
She added that the federal government will submit a formal petition to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia seeking royal consent to officially open the new judicial landmark.

Title: Fahmi: Only register for medicine delivery service through MoH to avoid scams on Facebook, TikTok
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Applications for the government's medicine delivery service (UMP) should be done only through the Ministry of Health, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today as he cautioned against possible scam attempts.
"Registration for the UMP programme is only conducted through KKM facilities, not via TikTok or Facebook accounts," the minister told reporters after launching the initiative here.
"I remind everyone there is no registration process other than at health clinics or Ministry of Health facilities only."
Patients in Malaysia will soon be able to receive their follow-up medication delivered directly to their doorstep free of charge, following a joint funding initiative announced today by the Communications Ministry and the Health Ministry.
Starting Oct 1, eligible patients will enjoy fully subsidized shipping costs for their follow-up prescriptions for a duration of one year under the UMP programme.
"The initiative is introduced to encourage more patients to utilise digital healthcare services, while simultaneously improving access to follow-up medications without requiring them to physically visit health facilities," the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) said in a statement today.
Fahmi encouraged the public to seek more information, reiterating that registration for the programme is free.
"Registration for the UMP program is free and does not require any payment," he said.
Under the strategic partnership, the MCMC — acting in its capacity as the regulator of the country's postal sector — will coordinate the execution of the programme, while the MOH will manage patient eligibility and medication supply.
The physical delivery of the medications will be handled by Pos Malaysia Berhad.
The programme could benefit some 80,000 patients across the country each month, with estimated total shipping subsidy of RM5 million.

Title: Health minister: Mission is to transform healthcare within 15th Parliament timeframe
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 29 — Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad wants the national healthcare transformation agenda, including modernising the system and improving patient service delivery, to be completed within the 15th parliamentary term.
He said the Ministry of Health (MOH) faces a major challenge of not only keeping facilities ready but also ensuring healthcare delivery consistently meets the people’s needs.
The focus, he said, includes streamlining existing systems and improving healthcare delivery, with patient experience and journey among the key considerations in executing the ministry’s initiatives.
“Faced with various challenges in healthcare services and the service system, I am certainly among the ministers dealing with a plethora of problems. Our ministry is, by nature, first, facility-based, and second, service-based.
“As such, the challenge for me, my ministry, MOH secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, and Health director-general, Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab, is to ensure that in this 15th Parliament, I fulfil my ambition of building a modern healthcare system and delivery.
“Whatever the method, platform or initiative, I will deliver it as soon as possible,” he said at the launch of the Financing for the Medicine-by-Post Initiative (UMP) today.
Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, his deputy Teo Nie Ching, and Ministry of Communications secretary-general, Datuk Abdul Halim Hamzah.
Dzulkefly said MOH faces increasingly complex challenges, including food safety and quality, mental health and planetary health.
To strengthen healthcare transformation, he said, the Ministry is also focusing on digitalisation and interoperability across health systems and facilities, including electronic medical records that let public and private facilities share data.
Dzulkefly added that MOH wants healthcare delivery closer to the community and less dependent on hospitals or health facilities for matters that can be handled through alternatives.
He cited UMP as an example that allows patients to obtain follow-up medication without visiting a health facility solely to collect medicine.
“This is the patient experience. We want better treatment and, ultimately, less congestion at hospitals,” he said.
Dzulkefly said efforts to improve follow-up medicine delivery are nothing new, with pharmacy initiatives rolled out in phases over the past decade.
These include Drive-Through Pharmacy, Locker4U and the Local Follow-Up Medicine Supply Centre, as well as UMP and the MyUbat app, to ease the management of follow-up supplies and save patients time and money.
“Healthcare services must not only be available but easily accessible to all Malaysians. That is why we want to deliver on this. That is the mission of the year,” he said. — Bernama

Title: PM Anwar congratulates Kelantan Sultan on 57th birthday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim extended his heartfelt congratulations to the Sultan of Kelantan, Sultan Muhammad V, on the occasion of the ruler’s 57th birthday.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar prayed that Sultan Muhammad V and the entire royal family will always be blessed with His grace and guidance.
“May Allah protect Tuanku in this world and the hereafter. Daulat Tuanku,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Lawmakers welcome national suicide registry, urge strict service standards for crisis helplines
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Three DAP lawmakers have welcomed the launch of the National Suicide and Fatal Injury Registry Malaysia (NSFIRM) and the Ministry of Health’s Postvention Services Guidelines, while calling for stronger crisis helpline standards.
In a joint statement, Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Wuen and state assemblymen Lim Yi Wei (Kampung Tunku) and Michelle Ng Mei Sze (Subang Jaya) said the launch, three years after attempted suicide was decriminalised, reaffirms the government’s commitment to mental health.
They said that Malaysia previously lacked a systematic registry of suicide deaths and attempts. Suspected suicides may initially be classified as “sudden death”, and differences in reporting and investigation practices, along with stigma, have obscured the full picture.
“NSFIRM can make this picture clearer through systematic analysis and incident trend monitoring.
“In the age of social media, incident trend monitoring is crucial. Viral trends can become a vehicle for self-harm among vulnerable individuals, especially youth who lack safe spaces to express emotional distress, such as the TikTok ‘barcode’ trend,” they said.
They also welcomed commitments by major media players at the June 8 ministerial dialogue on ethical suicide reporting, including listing helplines. However, they cautioned that “many helplines mean little if nobody picks up the phone”.
They urged the Health Ministry, through the National Centre of Excellence for Mental Health, to implement performance indicators for helplines such as Talian Kasih 15999, Talian HEAL 15555 and Befrienders. These include answer and abandonment rates, waiting times, staffing across shifts and multilingual availability.
The trio also called for the guidelines to be coordinated with proposed civil service mental health guidelines, ensuring first responders are trained to record data and receive psychosocial support themselves.

Title: Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir sworn in as senator
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri today took his oath of office as a Senator representing the state for a three-year term from Sept 10, 2026 to Sept 9, 2029.
Mohamad Hairul Amir, 38, was sworn in before Dewan Negara President Datuk Awang Bemee Awang Ali Basah at a ceremony held at the Senate here.
He was appointed to fill the vacancy left by Amanah vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof, whose term as Senator ended on May 24.
On September 10, the Perak State Legislative Assembly elected Mohamad Hairul Amir, who is also chief special officer at the Office of the Tambun MP, following a motion tabled by Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad under Article 45(1)(a) of the Federal Constitution.
Meanwhile, Awang Bemee, in his speech, said Mohamad Hairul Amir’s broad experience spanning political leadership, public administration, government relations, community development and corporate governance would bring valuable insights to Senate debates and proceedings.
“His involvement in statutory bodies and government-linked companies (GLCs), as well as his roles on independent audit committees and private sector boards, has further broadened his experience in governance, management, accountability and integrity,” he said.
Awang Bemee hoped Mohamad Hairul Amir would draw on his wealth of experience to contribute constructively in discharging his duties as a Senator.
Meanwhile, he said the Dewan Negara would continue to play a pivotal role in strengthening Malaysia’s parliamentary institution, including through the implementation of the Parliamentary Service Act 2025, which, among other things, seeks to reinforce the principle of separation of powers and enhance the effectiveness of Parliament’s checks and balances.
He said the move was crucial to strengthening Parliament’s autonomy and standing, enabling it to fulfil its role effectively, independently and credibly within the country’s democratic system.
“We want the Dewan Negara to be an institution that voices the concerns of the people and the states, scrutinises national policies and legislation, and strengthens the principle of checks and balances within the parliamentary democratic system,” he said.
According to the parliamentary calendar, the Dewan Negara will convene for the Third Meeting of the Fifth Session of the 15th Parliament from November 30 to December 22. — Bernama

Title: Loke: Transport Ministry to centralise bunkering licences from February 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — The Transport Ministry will assume sole authority for approving bunkering licences and related permits starting February 1, 2027.
Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said that centralising these approvals will provide operators with a single point of accountability and ensure more consistent decisions regarding safety, fuel quality, and environmental protection.
“I consider this as one of the major achievements by MOT because I have been minister of transport for a number of years.
“When we always talk about bunkering, we know that one of the key challenges and problems are the red tapes where a simple permit needs approval from multiple agencies and ministries.
“So we have got many cabinet approvals to ensure that all the processes are streamlined and we only need to go through one single agency under the Ministry of Transport. This will help to boost our bunkering sector, hopefully,” Loke said while officiating Malaysia Maritime Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.
This reform is part of a broader strategy to build a competitive bunkering sector capable of meeting modern shipping demands and preparing Malaysia for the transition to cleaner marine fuels.
Loke also revealed that the ministry is partnering with Australia to develop a policy and legal framework for green bunkering, focusing on fuels such as LNG, biofuels, and methanol.
“This work also supports a wider international commitment. In the International Maritime Organisation's 2023 Greenhouse Gas Strategy calls for zero or near-zero emission fuels and technologies to account for at least 5 per cent of the energy use by international shipping by 2030, with a target of 10 per cent.
“Malaysia intends to be ready to support ships as that transition gathers pace,” he said.

Title: PM: Malaysians should have the choice to work past 60, ageing population needs options
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — With Malaysia expected to be an aged nation by 2048, the focus should not only be on ensuring sufficient retirement savings but also ensuring people have the choice to work past age 60, the prime minister said today.
In Malaysia, the minimum retirement age for the private sector and the mandatory retirement age for civil servants are both currently at age 60.
In his speech, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said those who want to work after age 60 should be given the choice, but did not say whether there are plans to raise the minimum or mandatory retirement age.
“Raising the floor is only half the work. We must also raise the ceiling by ensuring that longer lives are lived with agency, connection and purpose.
“Those who are capable and wish to continue working beyond 60 should have the opportunity to do so. This is about choice, not compulsion,” he said in his speech at the International Social Wellbeing Conference 2026 here, which was read out on his behalf by Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
Anwar’s raising the floor remark alludes to his earlier comments in his speech, including having adequate savings and sustainable income for retirement.
Anwar pointed out that allowing work beyond 60 or such age-friendly employment can “retain experience, strengthen organisations and allow people to remain economically active on terms that respect their circumstances.”
Anwar said older people can still give valuable contributions to society, even if these may not appear in economic statistics.
“Experience, judgment and accumulated knowledge remain valuable assets to society,” he said.
He gave examples such as a retired teacher who mentors students, a grandparent supporting a working family, and a community leader who helps strengthen social cohesion.
“We must raise the floor so that every Malaysian can age with dignity and security. We must also raise the ceiling so that longer lives remain years of purpose, contribution and connection. And we must shorten the distance between policy and delivery,” he said in concluding his speech.
Earlier in his speech, Anwar said Malaysians are living longer, and the key question for the country is how to ensure longer lives are lived with dignity, financial security, good health and purpose.

Title: Negeri Sembilan MB meets Tuanku Muhriz amid royal dispute
Article:
SEREMBAN, Sept 29 — Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was reportedly granted an audience with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negeri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Hinggap here today amid the state’s ongoing constitutional and customary dispute.
According to
Berita Harian
, Ismail arrived at the palace at about 10.50am, while the vehicle carrying Tuanku Muhriz entered the grounds about 10 minutes later.
The meeting was also understood to have been attended by Undang Luak Sungei Ujong Datuk Klana Petra Muhammad Faris Johari, Undang Luak Rembau Datuk Sedia Raja Hassan Ab Hamid and Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad.
Berita Harian
reported that the audience was reportedly related to the ongoing dispute, including the revocation of the appointments of 10 state executive councillors.
Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had recently urged Ismail to meet Tuanku Muhriz and the Undang Yang Empat to seek a resolution to the dispute.
Zahid also called for discussions with the Tunku Besar Tampin, Datuk Shahbandar and other customary leaders, taking into account the Negeri Sembilan state constitution, customs and relevant regulations.
Yesterday, Bukit Aman police completed recording statements from the 10 former state executive councillors and several other individuals in connection with the state’s ongoing palace crisis.

Title: Loke says will stay as transport minister until Najib house arrest begins
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — Anthony Loke Siew Fook today said that he will stay on as transport minister until former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak begins his house arrest.
He said that he had submitted his resignation letter to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yesterday, when they had discussed the matter further.
“During the discussion, he asked me to continue carrying out my duties for the time being.
“He will make a decision, but I said that there also needs to be a timeframe. So, the timeframe is that when Najib returns home, my resignation will take effect,” Loke told reporters after officiating Malaysia Maritime Week 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre.
The DAP secretary-general explained that his resignation is a party decision, conveying the DAP's disagreement with the conditional pardon that allows Najib to serve the remainder of his prison term at home.
Anwar had pointed this out during their meeting yesterday, Loke said, and suggested that the latter should remain in his so long as the house arrest was not yet effected.
While Loke acknowledged he is unsure of the exact date Najib will be released, he stipulated that his departure is tied directly to that event.
“Maybe he will be released tomorrow. Who knows? How would we know? I also do not know when he will be released,” he said.
Loke also reiterated that the DAP will remain part of the federal unity government, with its other ministers continuing to serve in the Cabinet.
Earlier this month, His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, the King of Malaysia, consented to granting a conditional pardon to Najib, allowing him to serve the remainder of his jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
This pardon is subject to Najib settling a RM50 million fine.
Najib has been serving a 12-year jail term at Kajang Prison following his conviction in the SRC International case in August 2022.
Previously in 2024, the Pardons Board had already halved his sentence to six years and reduced his fine from RM210 million to RM50 million.

Title: High Court finds Putrajaya, Selangor authorities liable for Taman Sri Muda flood devastation
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Sept 29 — The High Court has found the Malaysian government liable for damages caused by the catastrophic 2021 floods that devastated Taman Sri Muda in Shah Alam, citing a failure to promptly escalate disaster response and maintain effective mitigation systems.
Judicial Commissioner Shoba Rajah Dorai Rajah allowed the lawsuit filed by 50 residents, ruling that they had proven their claims of negligence and breach of duty by the defendants.
The respondents included the government of Malaysia, the director-general of the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma), the minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Special Functions), the director-general of the Malaysian Meteorological Department (METMalaysia), and the minister of environment and water.
The court also found the director-general of the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) and the Shah Alam City Council (MBSA) jointly liable with the federal government.
“The court therefore holds that the plaintiffs have established a foreseeable duty of care arising from the defendants’ operational functions and disaster-management responsibilities,” Shoba said.
The court rejected the defendants’ attempt to use an “act of God” defence, ruling it inapplicable when reasonable human intervention could have mitigated the disaster.
“Once an agency undertakes meteorological monitoring and national rescue operations, it is required to exercise reasonable competence in carrying out those functions.
“The defence based on unforeseeability is therefore limited to circumstances in which no reasonable human intervention could have prevented or mitigated the consequences,” she said.
The ruling noted that while technical data confirmed the unprecedented rainfall on December 18, 2021, the state possessed the means to detect the severity of the event but failed to translate that data into an actionable plan to protect citizens.
Consequently, the court accepted that liability for the operational failures of Nadma and METMalaysia rested with the federal government.
“Nadma failed to escalate the disaster response, maintain a Disaster Operations Control Centre (PKOB) and deploy the Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) unit effectively (which affected the timely provision of rescue assistance).
“METMalaysia failed to issue timely warnings at the appropriate danger category despite its forecast activity benchmarks,” she said.
The court identified a systemic collapse in disaster management, including the lack of public awareness programmes in Taman Sri Muda despite its known status as a flood-prone area, and a failure to identify the correct disaster tier, which delayed critical intervention.
Bureaucratic failures further compounded the crisis, with delays in transmitting information from district to state levels and a lack of appointed liaison officers to coordinate the response. This left search-and-rescue efforts largely to non-governmental organisations and local community members.
Regarding DID Selangor, Shoba ruled that the agency could not avoid liability simply because rainfall exceeded infrastructure benchmarks.
“Once the assets were constructed and placed into operation, DID assumed a continuing duty to maintain, upgrade and operate them with reasonable competence.
“The defence that the capacity of the infrastructure had been exceeded is therefore insufficient where operational failures have compounded the problem,” she said.
Similarly, MBSA was found unable to evade its statutory obligations by claiming that retention ponds and primary infrastructure belonged to DID. The court held that ownership did not negate MBSA’s independent duty under street, drainage, and building legislation to maintain the public drainage system within its jurisdiction.
The court fixed October 6 for case management to determine a hearing date for the assessment of damages.
The 50 residents were represented by James Joshua Paulra, Regine Ng, and Ahmad Badri. Senior federal counsels Mohammad Al-Saifi Hashim, Nurul Farhana Khalid, and Liew Horng Bin appeared for the federal government, while state legal counsel Faris Shah Kamarulzaman and lawyer Norazalina Hairuddin appeared for JPS Selangor and MBSA respectively.

Title: Avoid the F1 rush: AirAsia advises extra KLIA travel time Oct 2-4
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 29 — AirAsia advises all guests travelling through the Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 to plan their journey, as higher passenger volumes and heavier traffic are expected in conjunction with the Formula 1 race weekend at Sepang International Circuit from Oct 2 to 4.
The airlines said guests are advised to arrive at the airport at least three hours before the scheduled departure time for international flights and two hours before the scheduled departure time for domestic flights.
“All guests, including those travelling under group bookings, are strongly encouraged to complete self check-in via the AirAsia MOVE app or our website.  Self check-in is available from 14 days up to one hour before the scheduled departure time,” it said in a statement, adding that check-in counters are designated for guests requiring reduced mobility assistance and other special assistance needs.
Besides, Malaysian passport holders travelling internationally are encouraged to use the MyNIISe or MyBorderPass app to facilitate a smoother immigration clearance process at KLIA Terminal 2, it said.
It added that guests are encouraged to use the Express Rail Link (ERL) to facilitate convenient and reliable public transport access to KLIA2. Guests are also advised to stay updated on traffic advisories and road closure announcements from the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), and plan alternative routes where necessary.
“Guests travelling during the race weekend are advised to allow additional travel time to the airport due to anticipated congestion on major routes leading to KLIA Terminal 2 and the Sepang International Circuit,” it said.
AirAsia also encourages guests to follow its official social media channels for the latest travel advisories. — Bernama
